narrative: The model estimates a 22% probability that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty—roughly one in five students with a similar profile would not pass—but it is still high enough that the school requires remedial courses to reduce the risk. The strongest factors in the model’s explanation were your record of no past class failures, your receipt of school educational support, and your intention to pursue higher education. All three pushed the estimate toward passing, not failing. Your zero past failures matches the average for students who passed; wanting higher education is also typical of passers; and although school support is uncommon among passers, it counted in your favor. Because the top-ranked factors were protective, the fail prediction is not driven by those strengths. Instead, other, less influential parts of your profile—such as very high weekend alcohol consumption and a commute over 60 minutes—appear to have outweighed them. To improve, keep your attendance and study routine steady, make full use of the school support available, and reduce weekend drinking and the strain of your long commute where possible. Speaking with a counselor about time management and support options would help turn these protective factors into a stronger pass outcome.
